ElringKlinger AG Launches Advanced Thermal Management System for Electric Vehicles

ElringKlinger AG, a prominent supplier in the German automotive industry, unveiled its latest thermal management system for electric vehicles at a launch event in Dettingen an der Erms on Thursday. The new system, which focuses on enhancing the efficiency and longevity of electric vehicle batteries, is set to be available to automotive manufacturers across Europe beginning next quarter.

The product, developed over two years by ElringKlinger AG’s engineering teams, uses advanced phase-change materials and smart sensors to optimize temperature regulation during both rapid charging and high-performance driving. Company officials say this innovation will help address a key challenge for vehicle manufacturers as electrification accelerates in the global automotive market.

“Our new thermal management system is a crucial step forward for electric mobility,” said Dr. Stefan Wolf, CEO of ElringKlinger AG, during the presentation. “It enables better energy efficiency and supports battery durability, which are vital factors for the next generation of electric vehicles.”

Analysts welcomed the announcement, noting that thermal management is gaining strategic importance as demand for electric vehicles rises. “Effective battery cooling systems are essential for safety and performance,” commented Martina Schäfer, an automotive technology analyst at AutoTrend Research. “ElringKlinger’s solution could provide a competitive edge for OEMs looking to differentiate their EV offerings.”

The product launch comes amid strong growth in Germany’s electric vehicle market, with industry data showing a 14% increase in EV registrations in the first half of the year. The German Automotive Association (VDA) has emphasized the need for continual innovation to support this transition. “Thermal management solutions like this are indispensable as vehicles become more electrified,” said a VDA spokesperson.

ElringKlinger AG’s new system will initially be produced at its facility in Baden-Württemberg, with plans to scale up output in response to customer demand. The company also announced that it is in discussions with several European carmakers to integrate the technology into upcoming vehicle models.
